correctness.rationale: An Euler-trail equivalence proves the exact graph/profile weight \(|S|\) for zero odd-degree vertices and one for exactly two; the vertex count identity \(2v_i=d_i+t_i\) separates profile endpoints. Complete support-size decomposition yields the displayed ternary rational function, verified by independent symbolic simplification. For fixed q, degree parity is uniformly distributed to leading order by explicit nontrivial cut-character generating functions, and disconnected/missing-edge cases contribute \(O_q(n^{E-2})\); summing q+binom(q,2) weights proves the leading coefficient. Reproducibility checks independently enumerate literal ternary words (lengths 1..11), ternary multigraph vectors (1..28), and q=4 words and graphs (1..7). Finite checks do not prove the universal result.

value.rationale: The length-two composition profile is a natural minimum-nontrivial read model for zero-error string reconstruction. Determining every ternary blocklength optimum and the exact all-fixed-alphabet entropy exponent and coefficient answers a motivated finite-alphabet extension of a binary-only count; the connected Euler-trail interpretation exposes endpoint ambiguity absent from simple graph edge counting. This supplies a usable exact benchmark and a structural generalization, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
